system:
You are the S1 seat (clarify & translate) of the HDCS loop. Human input may arrive in any register; every artifact you emit is machine-facing hcdl: domain-locked ultra-technical register + mathematical notation, zero filler.

REGISTER. Detect the input's domain and lock it as reg: {domain: <tag>, canon: <1-line vocabulary guide naming the canonical technical vocabulary field>}. A programming task thinks in code-adjacent nouns — exact identifiers, API names, formal terms; never generic smart-sounding filler. Quality principle: precise post-grad technical terms replace vague guesswork — the packet must reconstruct the requirements exactly.

NOTATION. -> leads-to/results-in; := defined-as; => therefore; ∀ for-all; ∃ exists; ∈ in; ∧ and; ∨ or; ¬ not; Δ change; ∴ hence; ∵ because; ≥ ≤. Report keys (ASCII-exact): +done -resolved +open +validation. State marker (ASCII-exact): S_0 + Delta -> S_1. Filler ban: "in order to", "please note", "it should be noted", "essentially" -> delete or notate. Abbreviations: registry S1..S5, P1, B1, QG, RR, NR, FA, DEC always safe; anything else binds at first use via := before bare reuse; never bind a form colliding with the reg canon (cs-programming reserves PC/GC/AST); never abbreviate inside must_keep.

CONSTANTS ARE LITERAL — copy verbatim, they mark schema conformance, never your verdict:
- workflow.gate is ALWAYS exactly: READY|NOT_READY   (your actual readiness judgment goes in handoff.report)
- handoff.state is ALWAYS exactly: S_0 + Delta -> S_1
Correct example line: workflow: {phases: [plan, scoped-build, verify, deliver], builders: dynamic, verifier: decorrelated, gate: READY|NOT_READY, max_fix_cycles: 2}

FORCED BINARY. Either every remaining ambiguity is resolved by the recorded operator answers (then certify no-ambiguity with evidence inside resolved:), or record the questions you would ask — WHERE: each remaining question is a resolved: entry of the form `Q<i>: <question> -> A: OPEN` AND is reflected in handoff.report's +open item. NEVER create a top-level +open key; the packet has exactly the nine top-level keys below, nothing else.

MUST_KEEP. The task input carries MUST_KEEP: lines (human non-negotiables). Each must appear VERBATIM as a must_keep: list entry — a validator probes for these exact phrases.

OUTPUT — one hdcs/1 state packet, exact top-level keys, nothing else:
reg: {domain: <tag>, canon: <1-line vocabulary guide>}
intent: <locked goal in hcdl, <=8 lines>
must_keep: [<human non-negotiables, verbatim-faithful>]
resolved: [<clarification Q->A records, including operator answers folded in>]
workflow: {phases: [plan, scoped-build, verify, deliver], builders: dynamic, verifier: decorrelated, gate: READY|NOT_READY, max_fix_cycles: 2}
handoff: {state: S_0 + Delta -> S_1, report: [+done, -resolved, +open, +validation]}
constraints: [<hard constraints; cite no_resurrect ids>]
paths: [<canonical paths — lists, never repeated mapping keys>]
budgets: {tokens: <n|estimate>, lines: 60, fix_cycles: 2, questions: 2}
Multi-value fields are lists — repeated mapping keys silently drop entries on parse (the defect class this very task guards against). Wrap the packet in a single ```yaml fence. No prose outside the fence.

## REASONING BUDGET: NONE
Think as long as the task demands. The hcdl packet is your OUTPUT ENCODING, not a reasoning limit — reason freely in whatever depth you need, then COMPRESS your conclusions into the register. Never truncate reasoning to fit line counts; overflow belongs in context.hcdl.

## CONTEXT REGISTER (mandatory second section)
After thinking, emit `=== context.hcdl ===` (before the packet fence) containing the DISTILLED OPERATIVE LAW of the task in hcdl notation: defs, invariants (each operator ruling as a resolved claim, e.g. `A5_mirror: ∀ path -> DST end state == SRC end state, recursive`), open items. This is the register of record every downstream worker reads natively — keep it current-law only, no debate history. The packet then summarizes state/route; detail lives here.

## OUTPUT TERMINATION (hard requirement)
Reasoning is free but MUST TERMINATE inside the response token budget. Budget discipline: spend at most ~1/3 of your budget reasoning; conclusions compress INTO context.hcdl (the register holds reasoning, not a preamble). If budget runs tight, cut prose — never cut the two sections. A response that hits the token cap before emitting `=== context.hcdl ===` and the yaml fence is a total failure.

## REASONING FREEDOM (supersedes OUTPUT TERMINATION above)
Operator ruling: there is NO thinking cap in prod. Think as long as the task demands — the only constraints are that you reason IN the register (hcdl notation, conclusions land in context.hcdl) and follow the house rules. The required sections are non-negotiable; the path to them is yours.

## report: KEY — EXACT SHAPE (common failure)
`report:` is a LITERAL ARRAY of the four section NAMES — never an object, never filled with content:
  report: [+done, -resolved, +open, +validation]
Content for those sections lives in the report body (the lines after), not in the key. If the validator echoes "want [+done,-resolved,+open,+validation]", it is telling you the key must be exactly this array.
user:
Task: operator runbook for the run-001 hermes-context sync tool

Run 001 delivered a working sync artifact (runs/001-hermes-context-timer/artifact/):
sync-hermes-context.sh plus systemd user units. New operators have nothing that
explains how to live with it. Write that document.

Deliverable (single file): RUNBOOK.md — a runbook for a NEW operator with zero
prior context. Required sections, in order: What this tool does; Test before
installing (--dry-run); Install; Configure (change the source); Schedule
(systemd user timer); Verify a sync; Roll back a bad sync; Troubleshooting
(refusals and what their A-number citations mean).

System facts you must represent accurately (they are the accuracy bar):
env vars HERMES_CONTEXT_SRC / HERMES_CONTEXT_DST override the deployed defaults
(/opt/data/workspace/hermes-context/ -> /workspace/hermes-context/); --dry-run
performs zero writes; --verify exits nonzero on mirror mismatch; real runs log
one line to ~/.cache/hermes-context/; install path ~/.local/bin; units in
~/.config/systemd/user/; timer fires every 6 hours; refusals exit nonzero and
cite an A-number.

Artifact register (the run-001 artifact directory contains exactly these four
files; all of them are in-scope to teach: sync-hermes-context.sh,
hermes-context.service, hermes-context.timer, README.md). Install instructions
must not assume the target directories already exist (teach the mkdir -p or
install -D step). The rollback section must give a concrete data-restore action
for a bad sync (remove or re-sync HERMES_CONTEXT_DST from a known-good source),
not merely disabling the timer.

CLI and citation register (closed world, extracted verbatim from the tool):
- The tool's own flags are exactly --dry-run and --verify (anything else is a
  usage error, exit 2). The strings --checksum / --delete / --itemize-changes
  in the source are rsync's internal invocation flags, not tool flags.
- Behavior: a real sync is a one-way mirror that converges HERMES_CONTEXT_DST
  to HERMES_CONTEXT_SRC (recursive, removes stale extras in DST, preserves
  entry types and symlink targets, then re-verifies); --dry-run prints the
  plan and performs zero writes; --verify compares and exits 0 iff DST is an
  exact mirror, nonzero with an A9 citation otherwise; success exits 0.
- Refusal/exit citation register (cite only these, only where true):
  A23 set-but-empty env var, and unset falls back to the production defaults;
  A18 degenerate paths (empty, '.', resolving to '/');
  A12 SRC/DST same path, ancestor/descendant relation, or a symlink path
  component it refuses to follow or replace;
  A13 staging verification failed (DST left untouched);
  A14 staging path conflicts, including TMPDIR set but empty (TMPDIR may set
  the staging parent);
  A9 mirror-mismatch findings (content, type, symlink-target, stale extras).
  If a refusal's citation is not in this register, describe the condition
  without a citation.
- Known-good source means the configured HERMES_CONTEXT_SRC: after removing a
  bad HERMES_CONTEXT_DST, re-syncing from it is the documented restore.

Example rule: illustrative example paths for the OPERATOR's own files (e.g. a
source directory under the home directory) are allowed when clearly marked as
examples. Claims about the TOOL are still closed-world: no env var, flag,
default, or behavior beyond this facts block may be asserted as the tool's.

MUST_KEEP: documents HERMES_CONTEXT_SRC and HERMES_CONTEXT_DST exactly
MUST_KEEP: includes a --dry-run test the operator can run before installing
MUST_KEEP: states the documented rollback for a bad sync


=== OPERATOR ANSWERS ===
A1: Runbook target is the run-001 sync tool; the system-facts block in task.md is
    the accuracy contract; nothing else about the tool may be asserted.
A3: Plain imperative English; every hcdl register term (A-number, packet, seat)
    must be explained or omitted from the runbook body.
A4: No invented flags/env vars/paths. If the facts block does not name it, the
    runbook may not teach it.
A5: Document the tool AS DELIVERED (including its refusals), not an idealized version.
A6: Sections in the mandated order; every section non-empty; rollback section must
    name the concrete restore action, not "reinstall".
A7: S4 rubric: FAIL if any command in the runbook would fail as written against the
    run-001 artifact, or if a MUST_KEEP section is missing or hollow.

=== context.hcdl ===
def artifact := {sync-hermes-context.sh, hermes-context.service, hermes-context.timer, README.md} @ runs/001-hermes-context-timer/artifact/
def tool_flags := {--dry-run, --verify}; ∀ other token -> usage error exit 2 (rsync internal flags ¬ tool flags)
def env := {HERMES_CONTEXT_SRC := /opt/data/workspace/hermes-context/, HERMES_CONTEXT_DST := /workspace/hermes-context/}; set-but-empty -> A23; unset -> prod defaults
def behavior: real sync = one-way mirror, DST converges to SRC (recursive, removes stale DST extras, preserves types ∧ symlink targets), staging verify -> A13 on fail (DST untouched); --dry-run zero writes; --verify exit 0 iff exact mirror else nonzero + A9
def citations := {A23 set-but-empty env, A18 degenerate paths (∅, '.', '/'), A12 path identity/ancestor/symlink component, A13 staging verify fail, A14 staging path conflict incl TMPDIR set-but-empty, A9 mirror mismatch} — closed world; unknown citations -> describe condition, no A-number
def install := mkdir -p/install -D required (dirs ∉ assumed); bin -> ~/.local/bin; units -> ~/.config/systemd/user/; timer period := 6h
A1: accuracy contract := system-facts block, closed-world tool claims only
A3: register := plain imperative; hcdl terms (A-number etc.) explained or omitted
A4: no invented flags/env/paths/defaults
A5: document tool as delivered incl refusals
A6: sections ordered [What this tool does, Test before installing (--dry-run), Install, Configure, Schedule, Verify a sync, Roll back a bad sync, Troubleshooting]; ∀ section non-empty; rollback = remove/re-sync DST from HERMES_CONTEXT_SRC (concrete restore)
A7: validation := S4 rubric — FAIL iff ∃ command failing as written vs artifact ∨ MUST_KEEP hollow/missing
INV_MK1: runbook names HERMES_CONTEXT_SRC ∧ HERMES_CONTEXT_DST exactly
INV_MK2: runbook includes pre-install --dry-run test
INV_MK3: runbook states documented rollback for bad sync
open: none
